title: Consistency Pact
concept: A private weekly look at the gap between what you say you value and what you did, and one change to close it, without your partner having to check.
whenToUse: Once a week, on your own. Also after a promise that mattered, or alongside a shared Proof item while you rebuild trust.
steps: What you say: what do you say you value? Write it down.
What you meant to do: what did you plan to do this week?
What actually happened: where was the gap?
One change: pick one thing to do differently next week that you could point to.
Keep it private unless you choose to share it. Your own notes, thoughts and answers are never owed.
Broke a shared agreement? Tell your partner. Telling them is part of the partnership, and this pact never replaces it.

phrases.text: Next week I will ___ (something you could point to).

working: Tuesday, A is curt about the gas bill and lets it sit till Thursday. A’s change: a same-day text, “That was sharp, sorry.” Friday, A sends it before lunch.
notWorking: B breaks an agreement about money and, instead of telling A, writes it up in a private pact. Writing it down is fine; hiding the broken agreement from A isn’t.
activity: Write your own private pact. Look at it once a week for three weeks.
